info.title: Judgment Pack Runner local pilot
info.description: Single local installation owner, one fixed pack release per job. Durable local schedules, file changes and authenticated event admission. Experimental evaluator; no external actions. Direct runner prefix /v1; owner-authenticated Desk proxy /api/operations. In service mode (jpack-runner serve --config) the control API is a long-running service's: with an identity configured, every request but GET /health carries an identity token in place of the owner bearer, and Runner speaks plain HTTP, terminating no TLS.

get.description: Runner's identity, health and capabilities. A capability names a feature a client can test for before using it; journal-backward means the journal routes accept tail and before. selected-profile-preparation means the selected-profile namespace and its routes under /retained-column/1/ (listSelectedProfiles, admitSelectedProfile, selectedPlanNextInputSource) are served. scope-identifiers means a job may be created under a scope identifier, which its records carry, the store-wide listings filter by, and every request that names one of them names (ScopeIdentifier). retries means a job may be created with a retry policy (RetryPolicy), and an interrupted run may be retried (retryRun). run-results means a finished run carries counts (RunCounts) and, when it ended without a decision, an errorClass (ErrorClass), as an occurrence that ended without a run carries its errorClass; a run's end is journaled with them; and the runs listings take outcome and errorClass, and the journal routes outcome, errorClass and kind, as filters. A Runner without it ignores those parameters and answers every record. With an input root bound, inputRootReplacementCharacter says whether the binding contains U+FFFD, which may be a literal character or may have replaced a byte lost before the path reached Runner (Runner cannot tell which), and inputRootExists whether the bound root exists as a directory, or inputRootUnreadable, in its place, that the bound root's status could not be read for a reason other than its absence; without one, all are absent. The boot line's and a relocation's path members (README, Paths are UTF-8) and every stored binding are valid UTF-8 with no NUL; a request or store outside that domain is refused before Runner serves (README, Paths are UTF-8).

Service mode only: whether Runner is healthy, for a probe that holds no credential. healthy is false, answered 503, once the dispatcher has stopped after a storage error. It says nothing else: not the store, its directory, the workspace, the owner or a digest; GET /status, which does, keeps its credential. A browser Origin is refused. A companion does not serve this route.

get.description: Trusted bootstrap and durable registered installation profiles with canonical digests. Imported fixtures never install authority. After them, each registered profile set aside when Runner opened its store: one an earlier Runner admitted and this Runner's form refuses on its own, such as a scoped page profile whose endpointScope entry RFC 0018 round 16 refuses. It is listed with state set-aside and the reason, its profile the stored bytes served compacted and JSON-escaped as every answer is; the store's row keeps them exactly. Its ID stays taken, it counts toward the 16 profiles, and a binding, job or run that names it is refused as input_profile_set_aside, naming it.

post.description: Trusted-host configuration only. Add one immutable profile (request at most 32 KiB) without restarting workers. Persist before visibility. An identical retry returns the same digest; changed contents under an existing ID are refused, and so is the ID of a profile set aside when Runner opened its store. At most 16 combined profiles, a set-aside one included; none is evicted. The store's row keeps every profile it holds as it holds it, a set-aside one byte for byte. Does not acquire data, change releases or authorize model execution. Bearer authentication is required and browser Origin requests are refused. The ID of a selected profile (admitSelectedProfile) is refused as 409 input_profile_selected.

get.description: Offline input lineage bundle. Trust the profiles and release digest independently. Does not establish sealed-session completeness or policy truth. Version 2, 3, 4 or 5 may be asked for, at most once (none asked is 2), and the run is served at the highest version up to the one asked whose material it holds, answered 200 either way, so read version from the body: version 3 adds the audit record's original bytes, version 4 also the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, and version 5 also the record's signature sidecar. A run the store no longer holds, whose entry the chain still names, is answered with 410 run_not_held, naming the entry's sequence. A run of a job with no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping, has no lineage: it is served from version 3 on, by the same steps, with inputs: not-mapped and no preparation, and is refused with 422 not_verified_mapping when it holds no audit record's bytes or version 2 (or none) is asked. A run whose release keeps a supplied reviewed-set lock that is no longer the bytes its digest names is refused with 500 store_error.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The export version asked for, at most once, in a well-formed query. Without it, or with 2: version 2, unchanged. With 3: version 3 when the run holds its audit record's bytes, and version 2 for a run that holds none (recorded before Runner kept them, or without an audit record). With 4: version 4 when the run also has an entry in the installation's chain of runs, and otherwise what 3 serves: a run recorded before Runner chained its runs has no entry and is unchained. With 5: version 5 when the run also keeps the signature sidecar of its audit record, and otherwise what 4 serves: a run recorded without a signing key, by a Runtime that cannot sign, or before Runner kept the sidecar, is unsigned. Anything else, or a malformed query, is refused with invalid_version. A run without lineage (no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping) has no version-2 export: with none or 2 it is refused with 422 not_verified_mapping, and with 3, 4 or 5 it is served as above, from version 3.

get.description: A finished run's attempt diagnostics: what its Runtime wrote to standard error, or standard output, when it evaluated the run, as written, up to the first 65,536 bytes (cut before a character the bound would split). A run still queued or running is refused with 409 run_not_finished. A run whose stream is not retained answers 404 no_diagnostics, with its state and what the store records of it (it expired in the queue, or never started); a missing file is never taken to say the Runtime did not run. The stream is read through the attempts directory Runner holds, and Runner serves only the file it looked at and then opened: the run's directory and the stream are each looked at without following a link, and checked on the opened descriptor to be that same object, a directory or a regular file private to the operator. A link when Runner looks, a file or directory others may read, or a name that resolves to any other object when opened is refused with 500 diagnostics_refused, and nothing of it is served; a name that vanishes in between answers 404. The Runtime's own words, kept in the operator's store: they explain a run and establish nothing about it. A read writes no entry in the journal of job activity.

post.description: Queues an interrupted run again, as the same run (docs/design/retries.md, section 6). Its interrupted attempt is kept in attempts (runner-stopped, with endedAt its interruptedAt, or runner-restarted); the run returns to queued with startedAt, finishedAt, problem and interruptedAt cleared and attempt unchanged, and the dispatcher makes the next attempt, which evaluates into its own directory (attempts/<run>.<n>), leaving the first attempt's as it was. A retried trigger run is held to its queue deadline and to source freshness at dispatch, as every attempt is, and keeps its place in the store's order of insertion. The original event id, or Idempotency-Key, of the run returns the run as it now is and queues nothing. Journaled run.queued from interrupted, with the kept attempt; a refusal of a run the store holds is journaled admission.refused, request retry-run. The job's retry policy does not apply: a run is retried only when asked, up to 10 attempts. Refused under the manual-admission gate (manual_unsupported). A store's first retry raises its schema to 6.

get.description: The installation's chain of runs: every entry's line, exactly as stored, each ended by a newline, in sequence order. An entry binds one completed run's id to the SHA-256 of its audit record's exact bytes, chained by the Runtime's rules (trail, sequence, previous over the exact bytes of the line before). It is a trail file as the Runtime's audit verify reads one, and verify-run --chain reads it. Read in pages, as it stood at some moment during the reading; a failure after the answer began aborts the transfer. The operator keeps the chain: against the operator it establishes nothing without a checkpoint held independently.

post.description: Direct Runner requires owner bearer plus X-Trigger-Token; in service mode with an identity, an identity token in place of the owner bearer, and X-Trigger-Token as before. Desk exposes POST /api/job-events/{trigger} using only Authorization: Bearer <trigger-token>; browser Origin is refused. New deliveries must be no older than 5 minutes, at most 30 seconds in the future. Exact retries return the original occurrence; changed payloads with the same ID conflict. Accepted work may be skipped by overlap policy: inspect occurrence.state. While the local queue of pending occurrences is full a new delivery is refused with 429 queue_full, retryable, and nothing is admitted: the event ID stays unused, and the same bytes delivered again are admitted once the queue has room, while occurredAt is no older than 5 minutes; after that they are refused with 422 event_expired. An ID that an earlier Runner version recorded as skipped with reason queue-full still answers with that recorded occurrence. No Retry-After header is sent. The token that created an occurrence can read its result with readEventResult.

bearer.description: The owner bearer: a companion's boot line's token, or a service configuration's. In service mode with an identity, an identity token in its place: a JWT in compact form, at most 8192 bytes, from the configured issuer (iss), naming the configured audience (aud), for a subject the configuration lists (sub), signed with RS256, ES256 or EdDSA by a key of the configured key set, named by kid, with an expiry (exp) and, when present, a start (nbf), each held with 30 seconds' leeway. The owner bearer is not taken then. A refused token is answered 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and a message naming one reason, which never repeats the token. A token is a bearer credential: Runner keeps no record of the tokens it has taken, so one can be presented again until it expires.

preparation.description: Server-computed for v2; never trusted from a caller.

Input.description: Manual facts/evidence, v1 selected file, or ordered v2 case/file/gateway-operation mapping. Omit facts/evidence to use projection; supplied values must match. V2 verification requires installation profiles. A dialect of version 3 is read as version 2 is, its unbound sources bound at import (source.import).

pack.description: The pack's JSON text. The Core version it declares as specVersion selects its evaluator, exactly: 0.2.0-draft, 0.3.0 or 0.5.0 on an ordinary release check, and 0.2.0-draft or 0.3.0 on the selected retained-column path, which refuses 0.5.0 by name. Any other version is refused as 422 invalid_pack before anything is written. For a pack that declares 0.5.0, Runner first asks the pinned Runtime, through version --format json, whether it lists 0.5.0 among its supportedSpecVersions and as an evaluator capability with no stage whose supportedProfiles lists base (Runtime 0.44.0 and later do). An answer that does not say so, that has a duplicated member or a member named as one of these but for case, or that cannot be read, is refused as 422 runtime_core_unsupported before the Runtime is given the pack, and no release is saved.

matrix.description: Optional serialized Runtime matrix with saved expectations. Omit only when no saved tests exist. It is evaluated afresh against the frozen pack and Runtime.

requireComparableFacts.description: Check the release with the Runtime's requireComparableFacts (runtime ADR-0046). The configuration Runner generates for the release is then {"configVersion":"5","packs":{"target":{"path":"pack.json"}},"audit":{"dir":"audit"},"requireComparableFacts":true} in place of the configVersion 3 one, and its Runtime refuses every evaluation of the release, the sample's rehearsal included, in which a fact some comparison of the pack reads is present and of a JSON type that comparison can never match (JPS-FACTS-COMPARABLE-REQUIRED): such a sample fails the check as 422 preview_failed, and such a run fails. Saved tests run under a configuration of their own, which does not set it. Runner first asks the pinned Runtime, through packs schema --format json, whether it lists configVersion 5 among supportedConfigVersions (Runtime 0.25.0 and later do). An answer that does not say so, or cannot be read, is refused as 422 comparable_facts_unsupported before the Runtime is given the configuration, and no release is saved. Refused under manual admission as 409 manual_profile_unsupported. Written null, the request is refused as 400 invalid_request. Omitted or false, the release has the configVersion 3 configuration every earlier release has.

lock.description: The reviewed-set lock's exact bytes, as the Runtime's packs lock wrote it (runtime ADR-0019): 1 byte to 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) of UTF-8, the bound every Runtime reader of a lock applies. The limit is in bytes, not characters, so a lock of fewer than 1048576 characters can still exceed it.

id.description: The decision id the pack is locked under in the lock, in the form a Runtime configuration gives a decision id: lowercase letters and digits in words joined by single hyphens.

reviewedSet.description: Hold the release to a reviewed-set lock made outside Runner, such as the lock of the project the pack was reviewed in (runtime ADR-0072). Runner writes the lock beside the pack in the release's private directory and, before the pack is validated, asks the pinned Runtime packs covers --lock FILE --id ID --pack pack.json --format json, without --config. The release is checked only when the Runtime answers that the lock covers the pack's exact bytes under the id: exit 0, status valid, an empty list of findings, the id, the pack's digest and the lock's digest Runner gave, and an entry whose digest is the pack's. Otherwise the check is refused and no release is saved: 422 pack_not_in_reviewed_set, naming the Runtime's findings (such as lock-entry-missing or document-drift), when it says the lock does not cover them; 422 invalid_reviewed_set, naming the Runtime's code, one that begins JPS-LOCK- or JPS-RESOURCE-LOCK- (such as JPS-LOCK-SHAPE, JPS-LOCK-JSON or JPS-LOCK-VERSION), when it refuses to compare the lock; 500 store_error when it refuses with any other code, such as one about the pack file Runner wrote, or gives no answer, because it could not start or did not exit within its 30 seconds; and 422 reviewed_set_unsupported for any other answer, among them that of a Runtime before 0.41.0, which has no packs covers. A lock that is empty or larger than 1 MiB, or an id that is not of its form or is longer than 128 characters, is refused as 422 invalid_reviewed_set before anything is written. A refusal carries neither the lock's bytes nor the Runtime's messages. The check says that this lock pins these bytes under this id; it does not say that a project's configuration declares them, or that the lock is the one a given project holds. The lock is the caller's: a lock is a document anyone can write, so a release checked against one, its runs' reviewedSetOrigin supplied and an installation's requireSuppliedReviewedSet show only that some lock naming exactly these pack bytes was supplied with the release check. They are no control against whoever may call this route. A consumer that needs a particular reviewed set compares suppliedLockDigest, or the release's kept lock, with the digest of a lock it obtained from a source it trusts. The release keeps the lock as suppliedReviewedSet, and its runs say that their reviewed claim rests on it (Run.reviewedSetOrigin). The release's own configuration and lock are unchanged and are still all that an evaluation is given. Refused under manual admission as 409 manual_profile_unsupported. Written null, the request is refused as 400 invalid_request. Omitted, the release is checked as before.

scope.description: The scope identifier the job is created under, fixed for as long as the job exists. Absent, the job has none. Written null, empty or out of form, the creation is refused (invalid_scope). A repeated creation from the same release must name the same one.

retry.description: The job's retry policy. Absent, the job makes one attempt; a policy of maxAttempts 1 is that default, and the job is created as without one (no retry member, the store's schema unchanged). A retry that is not an object, a member that is not a whole number, a duplicate member, or a member no policy takes is refused by the body's strict reading (400 invalid_request). Written null, missing a member, out of bounds, or under a name that only folds to retry or to one of its members, the creation is refused (422 invalid_retry_policy). A policy is accepted on any job, since a job's triggers and release can change after it is created, and acts only on occurrences that acquire their input over a Gateway connection that is not durable: on any other job it has no effect, and with maxAttempts above 1 it still raises the store to schema 6. A repeated creation from the same release must name the same policy, or none. Refused under the manual-admission gate (manual_unsupported).

CreateJob.description: Requires explicit review. Only passed checks and explicitly reviewed not-run releases are admitted. Failed, incomplete or mismatched test evidence returns 409 release_not_ready. An installation booted with requireTestedReleases refuses a new job from a not-run release with 409 release_untested; repeating the creation of an existing job still returns it. An installation booted with requireComparableFacts refuses a new job from a release not checked with it, one whose config is not byte for byte the configuration Runner generates with it, with 409 release_comparable_facts_required; repeating the creation of an existing job still returns it, and its runs keep running. An installation booted with requireSuppliedReviewedSet refuses a new job from a release not checked against a supplied reviewed-set lock, or whose suppliedReviewedSet lock does not have its lockDigest, with 409 release_reviewed_set_required; repeating the creation of an existing job still returns it, and its runs keep running. Coverage never gates. Reusing an immutable release and name is idempotent. A new job from a release that names a profile set aside when Runner opened its store is refused as 422 input_profile_set_aside; repeating the creation of a job made before still returns it. A release, job or run that names a selected profile (admitSelectedProfile) is refused as 422 input_profile_selected: a selected profile is bound by selected preparation alone.

ScopeIdentifier.description: A scope identifier (docs/design/scope-identifiers.md): an opaque label of at least one code point and at most 128 bytes of UTF-8, not 128 characters (the gateway's bound, in bytes; maxLength counts characters, so none is stated), with no code point of General_Category Cc (tab and line feed among them), Co or Cn, Bidi_Control, Default_Ignorable_Code_Point or Noncharacter_Code_Point, as Unicode 15.0.0 assigns them; the gateway's rule for its own scope identifier, meant to stay the same. Compared as written, byte for byte: nothing is folded, trimmed or normalized. A label and a filter, not an authorization boundary: every request the API admits may name any scope, or none to list every scope's records.

RetryPolicy.description: A job's retry policy, fixed when the job is created (docs/design/retries.md). It governs the source acquisition of the job's occurrences over a Gateway connection that is not durable, and has no effect on a job's runs or on any other acquisition. An attempt whose call the gateway answered 429 or 503 in its own form (Content-Type application/json and a JSON object whose error member is a string), with no earlier call of the attempt answered, is made again after min(backoffSeconds × 2^(n−1), maxBackoffSeconds) seconds and no sooner than the answer's Retry-After, up to maxAttempts attempts. A wait past 3600 seconds or the occurrence's expiresAt fails the occurrence (retry-wait-too-long) rather than be shortened. Nothing else is retried: an answer of those statuses in any other form, such as a proxy's page, is uncertain and fails the occurrence. Absent, a job makes one attempt.

Attempt.description: One attempt: an occurrence's source acquisition, for a job with a retry policy, or a run's evaluation kept when the run was retried (docs/design/retries.md).

delaySeconds.description: The wait that preceded the attempt: 0 for the first, and for a run's attempt a caller asked for.

endedAt.description: Absent for an attempt Runner did not see end: one in flight at a restart.

outcome.description: succeeded; failed, a failure that is not retried; transient, a gateway answer of 429 or 503, retried while attempts are left; interrupted, in flight when Runner stopped. Absent while the attempt is in flight.

reason.description: An acquisition's error code (gateway_refused, gateway_unavailable and the others an acquisition answers), or, for a run's kept attempt, runner-stopped (Runner saw it stop) or runner-restarted (found running at a restart).

status.description: The gateway's answer's HTTP status, when the gateway answered with one other than 200.

retryAfterSeconds.description: The wait the gateway's Retry-After asked for, in whole seconds rounded up, when it carried one in either form.

scope.description: The scope identifier the job was created under; absent for a job created under none.

retry.description: The retry policy the job was created with, kept by every upgrade; absent for a job created without one.

config.description: The configuration Runner generated for the release, byte for byte, which every evaluation of it is given: {"configVersion":"3","packs":{"target":{"path":"pack.json"}},"audit":{"dir":"audit"}}, or the configVersion 5 one with requireComparableFacts for a release checked with it (PreviewRequest.requireComparableFacts). No project's jpack.json reaches a run.

lock.description: The release's own reviewed-set lock: what the pinned Runtime's packs lock wrote over the release's configuration and pack when the release was checked (runtime ADR-0019), which every evaluation of the release is given. It shows only that the pack has not changed since the release was made, not that a project reviewed the pack or that a project's lock names it.

suppliedReviewedSet.description: The reviewed-set lock the release was checked against, when its check supplied one (PreviewRequest.reviewedSet): the id the pack is locked under, the lock's exact bytes, and the SHA-256 digest of those bytes as sha256: and 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Each attempt of a run checks that the lock still has that digest, and is not evaluated otherwise. packs covers is not asked again: its answer depends only on these bytes, the pack's bytes and the pinned Runtime, which each attempt also checks by digest. A verification export of a run of the release is refused with 500 store_error when the lock no longer has that digest, and verify-run fails an export whose lock does not. Absent for a release checked without one, every earlier release among them.

requestedBy.description: Who requested the run: the owner, for a request that carried the owner bearer; for a request in service mode with an identity, the caller, written <issuer>#<subject> from the identity token it carried (an issuer holds no #, so the first # ends it); trigger:<id> for a run a trigger started; workflow for a workflow's. An Idempotency-Key is held within its requester's runs of the job: a caller's keys are its own, and the same subject from another issuer is another requester.

attempt.description: The run's current attempt: 0 while it was never started, 1 for its first, and one more for each retry a caller asked for (POST /v1/runs/{run}/retry).

auditBytes.description: The audit record exactly as the Runtime wrote it, without the newline that ends its line, in standard base64: the bytes a digest of the record, such as a gateway receipt's decision.recordDigest, is taken over. audit is the same record parsed, which Runner encodes again with other bytes. Every run Runner now records completed has them: an evaluation whose trail is not that one line, ended by a newline, is refused and its run fails. Absent for a run recorded before Runner kept them, for one Runner 0.4.0 completed without them, and for a run that did not complete. Not in run lists or briefs.

auditSignatures.description: The signature sidecar of the attempt's audit trail, signatures.jsonl, exactly as the Runtime wrote it, newlines included, in standard base64: the line signing the audit record, when the installation gave the Runtime a signing key (signingKey on the boot line) and it could sign. At most 16 KiB. Absent for a run recorded without a key, by a Runtime that cannot sign, or before Runner kept the sidecar; such a run is unsigned. What it holds is checked only by verify-run --public-key. Not in run lists or briefs.

interruptedAt.description: When Runner saw this run stop, at an orderly stop: the moment the evaluation it was in was cancelled. finishedAt keeps its meaning, the time Runner recorded the run's end. A run found running at a restart has none, since Runner did not see it stop: its run.interrupted journal entry gives the window the stop lies in. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports, whose version-2 readers decode strictly.

reason.description: Why a run ended without an evaluation, as a code: queue-expired, for an automatic run whose queue time ran out before the dispatcher reached it; binding-refused, for a mapping-v2 run whose Runtime refused the preparation's binding Runner passed (JPS-INVOCATION-BINDING), a defect of Runner, never retried without the binding; profile-set-aside, for a mapping-v2 run queued before a profile its release names was set aside when Runner opened its store, which never starts; its problem names the profile; prepared-by-earlier-runner, for a mapping-v2 run a Runner before 0.28.0 queued without its empty evidence-availability document, which this Runner does not evaluate, without the document or with {} filled in (MAPPING-V2.md). Its state stays failed, and its problem the sentence it was. Absent for every other run, and for a run that expired before Runner kept the code. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports.

signing.description: Whether the run's audit record is signed under the expected key: the public key of the installation's signing key as Runner read it at start, or the boot line's signingPublicKey, which that key must have, fixed for as long as it runs, and passed to each operational evaluation's Runtime as JPACK_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY. Held to the record's bytes the run keeps and the sidecar as kept (auditSignatures), by the check verify-run --public-key makes: signed when a valid signature under that key covers the record and no check failed, failed otherwise, with the reason in these exact words. A failed signing never withholds the decision: the run completes as an unsigned one does. Every run recorded completed with a signing key has it; absent for a run recorded without a key, one that did not complete, and one recorded before Runner kept it. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports, which carry the sidecar itself.

publicKey.description: The expected key, which a signed record is signed under. Present only when signed.

enum: The record's signature sidecar could not be read.
The record's signature sidecar names a key that is not the expected one.
The record's signature sidecar does not verify under the expected key.
The Runtime signed nothing: the key at the signing key's path is not the expected key.
The Runtime signed nothing, and the key at the signing key's path could not be read as a key.
reason.description: Why the signing failed. A sidecar that could not be read is never taken for no sidecar. Where no line signs the record, the key at the signing key's path, read again after the evaluation, says which of the last three: Runtime 0.30.0 and later refuse to sign with a seed that is not the expected key. Present only when failed. It names no path and no key.

binding.description: What Runner passed the Runtime of a completed mapping-v2 run's operational evaluation (MAPPING-V2, The preparation's binding): bound, when the Runtime was given the binding {"kind":"judgment-pack-runner/preparation/1","digest":"sha256:<SHA-256 of run.input.preparation in canonical form>"} and the run's audit record carries it byte for byte; unsupported-runtime, when the Runtime names a release before 0.31.0 and was given none; unversioned-runtime, when it names no release (0.0.0-dev, a build without its release's version), so that whether it takes a binding cannot be told, and was given none. Absent for a run without a mapping v2, one that did not complete, and one recorded before Runner passed a binding. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports, whose audit record carries the binding itself.

reviewedSetOrigin.description: Whose reviewed set the reviewed claim of this run's result or audit record is about, present when either says reviewed is true. release: the release's own lock (Release.lock), the only reviewed set a run is given; its reviewed: true shows only that the pack the run applied is byte for byte the pack the release froze. supplied: the release was also checked against a supplied reviewed-set lock (Release.suppliedReviewedSet), whose digest is suppliedLockDigest; when the release was checked, the pinned Runtime said that lock covers those same exact bytes under the id given. The lock is the caller's, a document anyone can write: supplied shows only that some lock naming exactly these pack bytes was supplied when the release was checked, and is no control against whoever may check a release. A consumer that needs a particular reviewed set compares suppliedLockDigest with the digest of a lock it obtained from a source it trusts. Read off the run and its release each time GET /runs/{run} or POST /jobs/{job}/runs serves it, so a run completed before Runner said it is served with it too; a run whose release cannot be read, or whose release's supplied lock is no longer the bytes its digest names, is not served (500 store_error). Not stored, and not in run lists, briefs or verification exports, which carry the release with its lock and any supplied reviewed set.

suppliedLockDigest.description: The digest of the supplied reviewed-set lock this run's reviewed claim rests on (Release.suppliedReviewedSet.lockDigest), present exactly when reviewedSetOrigin is supplied. It is not the reviewedSet.lockDigest of the run's result or record, which names the release's own lock.

scope.description: The scope identifier of the run's job, fixed when the run is queued; absent for a job created under none. Not part of a verification export.

attempts.description: The run's attempts before its current one, each kept, interrupted, when a caller retried the run. Absent for a run never retried. Served with the run; not in run lists, verification exports, nor the run's entry in the chain of runs.

counts.description: Present on a run that reached completed, failed or interrupted once Runner kept counts; absent on a run not yet ended, one queued again by a retry until its next end, and one that ended before. Served in run lists too. Not part of a verification export.

inputRootReplacementCharacter.description: Present when an input root is bound: whether the binding contains U+FFFD.

inputRootExists.description: Present when an input root is bound and its status could be read: whether the bound root exists as a directory. Absent when inputRootUnreadable is present.

inputRootUnreadable.description: Present, and true, when an input root is bound and its status could not be read for a reason other than its absence, such as a permission refused on a directory above it: whether it exists is not known, and inputRootExists is absent.

report.description: Retained Runtime packs test outputVersion 2, including rows and advisory coverage. Incomplete invocations may retain a diagnostic report.

mapping.description: The mapping. With import, omit it, and Runner makes it the bound dialect; or give that bound dialect, which must be the one the import makes. Runner makes it only when the member is absent: a mapping given beside import, {} and null included, that is not the bound dialect byte for byte in canonical form is refused as invalid_source_input.

mappingDigest.description: Runner-computed mapping digest; if supplied it must match.

retainedCaseJson.description: Sole exact case JSON text on the retained-column path, mutually exclusive with case. Stored text is not canonicalized.

SourceSnapshot.description: Retained JSON file (200,000 decoded bytes maximum). local-file requires selectedAt and forbids proof. google-drive requires the existing Desk DocumentObject proof with Drive selection, receipt response and sealed registry. Runner checks structural/byte binding, not cryptographic authenticity; consumers verify with their configured pin. No provider credentials. Snapshot max 1 MiB.

proof.description: Existing signed document acquisition and sealed registry contract; required for Google Drive.

factsText.description: Exact mapped facts JSON for consumers that cannot represent all JSON numbers losslessly.

evidenceText.description: Exact availability JSON; empty if omitted.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

source.description: JSON Pointer in the input object, or empty for the root.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

source.description: JSON Pointer in the input object, or empty for the root.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

source.description: JSON Pointer in the input object, or empty for the root.

sources.description: A research source's reconciliation (spec/dialect.md section 6.4): the earlier research sources it reads, distinct, beside a rule over {"current": its record, "sources": each named source's record, a skipped one absent}, with no copy and no unwrap. The rule guards each value it selects as found, names what every other status and absence does, writes no evidence, and ends with a clause that writes no fact and resolves nothing; anything else is refused, input-malformed.

SourceRead.description: copy or rule; a research source's read reads its record through a closed list of pointers (/fields, a declared field's entry, its status, its cites, its value and what is below it, and in a condition an observation's value) and never takes a value from under values, or is a reconciliation (sources and rule).

kind.description: operation and selected-file are version 2's, and a version-3 document's too, prepared as version 2 prepares them. research is a kind of dialect version 3 (spec/dialect.md sections 4.3 and 4.4): a recipe, bound to an AI profile and web profiles of class generated, prepared from the research record its caller retains, each retained response replayed under the profile it came through; Runner asks no model and reads no page. http, sql and web are kinds of dialect version 3 that Runner refuses by name: in a version-3 document, each is refused with a sentence naming the kind, and in a version-2 document, as an unsupported kind.

arguments.description: Frozen template; whole-value $param and integer-only $text. runAt is derivation-only. Under a profile whose adapter.name is adapter-http, a query, when present, is an object, not a template form, each of whose members is a string template (spec/dialect.md section 4.1): profile-mismatch otherwise.

platform.description: Version 3, unbound operation: the gateway catalog platform it is read through.

operation.description: Version 3, unbound operation: the operation of that platform's binding.

shape.description: Version 3, unbound operation: the shape that serves it. The profile it is bound to must be of this shape.

record.description: Version 3, unbound operation: the record it is written against, as a profile's adapter.name names it. The profile it is bound to must name this adapter.

method.description: Version 3, kind http: refused by name with its source.

path.description: Version 3, kind http: refused by name with its source.

query.description: Version 3, kind http: refused by name with its source.

body.description: Version 3, kind http: refused by name with its source.

headers.description: Version 3, kind http: refused by name with its source.

statement.description: Version 3, kind sql: refused by name with its source.

bindings.description: Version 3, kind sql: refused by name with its source.

url.description: Version 3, kind web: refused by name with its source.

question.description: Version 3, kind research: the question, a string template: a string, a $text whose placeholders name integer parameters, or a $param naming a parameter of type string or timestamp, never runAt. The source's request is its recipe, the question instantiated; it is recorded and never sent.

constraints.description: Version 3, kind research: the recipe's constraints, in the gateway canonical domain; kept as written.

model.description: Version 3, kind research: the model the recipe asks, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. The AI profile the source is bound to must declare this model: profile-mismatch otherwise.

evidence.description: Version 3, kind research: the evidence to retain, each instruction at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

fields.description: Version 3, kind research: the requested fields, in order, each exactly name (a non-empty string other than case, at most 64 UTF-8 bytes, distinct), type, required and description (at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes). The research record answers them.

capabilities.description: Version 3, kind research: the capabilities the recipe needs, distinct, in the order answer, search, page; answer is required.

webProfiles.description: Version 3, kind research, bound: a profile for each web capability the source asks for, exactly those, written even when empty. With profile and profileDigest, the AI profile for answer, all three or none: a research source published with none is bound at import (SourceInput.import).

MappingSource.description: A source of a dialect document. In version 3 an operation may be unbound: platform, operation, shape and record, all four, in place of profile and profileDigest (spec/dialect.md section 4.4); and a research source may be unbound, with none of profile, profileDigest and webProfiles. Runner prepares only a bound source: an unbound one is bound at import (SourceInput.import) and refused by name elsewhere. A research source is held to its recipe's form and the maxima of spec/dialect.md section 12, each refusal naming the specification's code at its end, input-malformed or input-over-bound; a profile it is bound to that this installation does not hold by that id and digest, that is not of class generated, declares no research capabilities, lacks the capability it is bound for or names another model is refused, profile-mismatch. The members of the kinds http, sql and web are read only so that a source of those kinds is refused for its kind. A version-2 source has none of the members of version 3.

profile.description: Explicit Base is required for retained-column conversions. Absent, ordinary legacy behavior and limits apply.

items.description: One entry: an endpoint prefix or https://*. Each entry is ASCII, each character from U+0021 to U+007E, so its 2048-character maxLength equals spec/dialect.md section 5.1's 2048 UTF-8 bytes.

endpointScope.description: An endpoint constraint in place of one exact endpoint, which is then null (spec/dialect.md section 5.1): 1 to 32 distinct endpoint prefixes, each https://, a DNS name of two or more labels, nothing, :443 or : with nothing, and an optional path beginning with /, with no user, query, fragment, IP literal or other port, no escaped slash or backslash (%2f, %2F, %5c, %5C) in the path, and no path segment that is a dot segment, or whose part before its first ;, %3b, %3B, %3f, %3F, %23 or %00 is one; or exactly https://*, admitted on a generated profile only. Only on shape http with adapter.name adapter-web; a generated profile carrying it declares research capabilities exactly ["page"]. A page receipt's acquisition.endpoint must match an entry: hosts equal with ASCII case folded, the three spellings of port 443 one port, the path a prefix at a literal / boundary, nothing decoded. The whole scope enters the profile's digest. It binds a research source's page assignment alone; an operation or a selected file bound to it is profile-mismatch.

research.description: What the channel serves of a research source's capabilities, distinct, in the order answer, search, page, and the model that answers, exactly when it serves answer (spec/dialect.md section 5.1): the form a gateway's web-search status row gives as research. The installation's declaration, pinned by the profile's digest; not an observation of the model. Runner refuses to start with one of another form.

conversionContracts.description: Trusted registered-profile metadata bound by the existing profile digest and approval. Absent entries grant no selected producer support.

receipt.description: Complete signed Gateway v3 acquisition receipt; Runner verifies the signed fields, profile and canonical result.

response.description: An acquisition, {result, receipt, salts}. A research source's result is its research record, exactly fields and responses (each retained response exactly profile, request, result, receipt and salts), and its receipt and salts are present exactly when the record came back through a gateway source; every other source's are required.

retainedResponseJson.description: Sole exact original signed response JSON text; excludes snapshot and response. It grants no signature, source or producer authority.

receipts.description: For an acquired research source: every citation it adds to the preparation's cites, in order, each retained response's and then the record's own when it has one; written even when empty. receipt is then the record's own citation, absent when it has none.

Preparation.description: A mapping-v2 run's verified preparation. From Runtime 0.31.0 on, the run's audit record binds it: the record's binding is {"kind":"judgment-pack-runner/preparation/1","digest":"sha256:<hex>"}, whose digest is the SHA-256 of this object with its members sorted by name, no insignificant whitespace, numbers as written, and strings escaped as Go's encoding/json escapes them, the form a frozen release is digested by. verify-run recomputes it from the export alone, compares the record's member as recorded, and reports binding: matches, mismatch, absent or foreign-kind, refusing a mismatch and a foreign kind (before any digest is compared), and, with --require-bound, a record without one. A binding that matches, in a record whose signature verifies, commits verifiedAt in the signed record: a program reading verify-run's report knows it when binding.status is matches and signature.status is signed, and unsignedFreshness keeps its name either way. Against the operator, who holds the key, only a witnessed chain shows a record signed again with a new binding.

version.description: The dialect document's version: 3 for a version-3 document, whose preparation is otherwise a version-2 document's.

cites.description: Every acquisition's citation, ordered by callIndex, those of one index in the order of sources; in a preparation with a research source, in the order of sources instead, each research source adding every retained response's citation in the order its record retains them, then the record's own (spec/dialect.md section 9.1).

VerificationBundle.description: Version 2, the export Runner has always made. It carries no original bytes of the audit record.

VerificationBundleV3.description: Version 3: version 2 with the audit record's bytes, as run.auditBytes, beside the parsed run.audit. Only a completed run that holds them is exported as version 3. verify-run checks that the bytes parse to run.audit and reports their SHA-256, the digest a gateway receipt would name for those bytes; that they are the bytes the Runtime wrote for this run is shown only by comparison with a digest held independently, such as a receipt's. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes member, whose bytes are held to 8 MiB.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

VerificationBundleV4.description: Version 4: version 3 with the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, as chain. Only a completed run that holds its audit record's bytes and has an entry is exported as version 4. verify-run checks that the entry names this run and the SHA-256 of run.auditBytes, and that the checkpoint is the entry's; along a supplied chain and against checkpoints held independently of the operator, it checks the entry's place in the chain. Without a held checkpoint it establishes nothing against the operator, who keeps the chain. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes and chain members; the entry is held to 1024 bytes. It carries no run.auditSignatures, which only version 5 does.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

VerificationBundleV5.description: Version 5: version 4 with the signature sidecar of the run's audit record, as run.auditSignatures. Only a completed run that has an entry in the installation's chain of runs and keeps a sidecar is exported as version 5. verify-run --public-key checks the record's signature under the key it is given, held first to the key check (no key of small order, no non-canonical encoding), by the Runtime guide's rule with the attempt's one-record trail known; --require-signed refuses a run that no valid signature covers. A valid signature shows only that whoever held the key signed these exact bytes: nothing against the operator, who holds the key, and nothing once the key is copied. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes, chain and run.auditSignatures members; the sidecar is held to 16 KiB.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

RunChainExport.description: A run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, and that entry's checkpoint, which a holder keeps. The checkpoint is a function of the entry's bytes.

entry.description: The entry's line exactly as stored, in standard base64: one JSON object of entryVersion "1", trail (32 lowercase hex characters), sequence (from 1), previous (the SHA-256 of the line before it, or of nothing for the first), kind "run", run (the run's id) and auditDigest (the SHA-256 of the run's audit record's exact bytes), in that order as Runner writes it. Read by its members, as JSON reads them.

Checkpoint.description: The Runtime's checkpoint (ADR-0047): a chain's identity, an entry's sequence, and the SHA-256 of that entry's exact line bytes. Its compact encoding, members in this order, is its RFC 8785 canonical form.

retainedColumn.description: Derived by Runner from the approved producer profile and mapping read. True requires all effective producer ceilings; it grants no producer authority.

PlannedSource.description: The next source to acquire. For a research source, the caller runs the recipe (arguments) through the profiles the source is bound to and supplies the research record it assembles from the responses it retains: Runner asks no model and reads no page.

Schedule.description: Intervals use elapsed time. Calendar schedules skip nonexistent local times and choose the first repeated time. End is exclusive. Kind-specific fields are mutually exclusive.

value.description: Exact JSON Input envelope; constants only. Source responses and computed preparation are forbidden.

path.description: Project-relative JSON input envelope or v2 case file.

AutomaticInput.description: mapped-sources supports v2 local files and installed Gateway operations. Retained source responses and interactive file grants are never reused.

preparationSeconds.description: Omit or use 0 for one hour on durable connections. Explicit waits require mapped-sources and all operation profiles installed as durable.

TriggerConfig.description: Event triggers take inputs from each delivery and forbid schedule/input/watch fields. Schedules require schedule and input. File triggers require a watched path used by their file inputs and a stability delay. Cloud triggers require cloud and input and forbid schedule/watch fields. For cloud, missed=latest delivers every signal before expiry; expiry starts at scheduledAt.

scope.description: The scope identifier of the trigger's job; absent for a job created under none.

reason.description: Why the occurrence ended, in a sentence, as before; or, for an occurrence of a job with a retry policy that the policy ended, attempt-limit-reached (its last attempt allowed was transient) or retry-wait-too-long (the next attempt's wait was past 3600 seconds or the occurrence's expiresAt).

scope.description: The scope identifier of the occurrence's job; absent for a job created under none.

attempts.description: The occurrence's source acquisition attempts, for a job with a retry policy; absent for a job without one.

nextAttemptAt.description: While an occurrence of a job with a retry policy waits for its next attempt (state accepted), the time of that attempt, which Runner does not make sooner. Absent otherwise.

token.description: Plaintext only when first enabling an event or rotating its credential; otherwise empty. Never retrievable later.

SourcePreparation.description: Public progress only. Checkpoint bytes, frozen operation requests and installed Gateway URLs remain private.

run.description: Present once the occurrence has a run.

CalculatorPin.description: The installation's statement that each allowed tool computes a deterministic function of the inputs it echoes and the tables it reports, calling no model. Only on a record MCP profile.

CalculationBinding.description: Required exactly when the operation's profile names a calculator. Binds each echoed input to a parameter of the source (never runAt) and each reported table to its maximum age in seconds.

CalculationInput.description: An input the calculator echoed, the parameter it is bound to, and where that parameter's value came from: the case or an earlier source, and the pointer.

JournalActor.description: Who Runner can say initiated a change. Never a person: Runner cannot know one. installation is whoever holds the owner bearer, named by the boot line's owner; a caller is a request in service mode that carried an identity token, named by the token's iss and sub as Runner checked them, never by the token: the issuer's name for a caller, not a person Runner knows; a trigger acts at a revision; a trigger-credential is an event delivery whose X-Trigger-Token was the trigger's current key, named by the revision the key was issued at (null for a key issued before the journal began), never by the token or its digest; a delivery refused after its credential was authenticated is that credential's, as it was then, even if the key is rotated before the refusal is recorded; a cloud-connection is a cloud signal Runner discarded; runner is Runner itself.

JournalConcerns.description: The ids a change is about, each present only where it applies. An entry that names a job also names its release.

JournalInterruption.description: An interruption's own time. seen true: Runner saw the stop, at at. seen false: Runner found the work at a restart and cannot know when it stopped; it was running at lastKnownRunning, the last time Runner recorded it alive (absent when the journal holds no such time), and had stopped by the restart, the runner.started entry at sequence restart.

JournalEntry.description: One entry of the journal of job activity (docs/design/activity-journal.md): one change of state Runner made, written in the transaction that made it, or a refused request to start work. The operator's own log: not chained, not signed, and binding nothing against the operator. It holds no inputs, secrets, tokens or digests of either. The members after reason are particular to kinds, as their descriptions say; a member added later raises entryVersion.

sequence.description: The entry's place in the journal, from 1, in the order changes committed: the cursor.

entryVersion.description: 5 for an entry that holds disposition, errorClass or counts, whatever its by, scope or attempt, which an entry of an earlier version never holds; 4 for any other entry that holds attempt, whatever its by or scope; 3 for any other entry about a job created under a scope identifier, whatever its by, which holds the member scope an entry of version 1 or 2 never holds; 2 for any other entry whose by is a caller, whose members issuer and subject an entry of version 1 never holds; 1 for every other entry. A reader that knows version 1 alone can tell by its version, before it reads by, an entry that holds a member it does not know: a 2 is a caller's, a 3 a scoped job's, a 4 holds an attempt, and a 5 a run's or an occurrence's end with its counts or class, whatever its by.

at.description: When Runner wrote the entry, by its own clock. Order is sequence, never at.

scope.description: The scope identifier of the job the entry concerns, on an entry of any kind about a job created under one; absent otherwise.

revision.description: The trigger revision: after the change, for a change of a trigger; the one an occurrence was admitted under, for the occurrence and its run.

from.description: The record's state before the change, for triggers (paused or enabled), occurrences and runs; null when the change created the record. Absent for a kind that concerns no record with a state.

to.description: The record's state after the change. Absent for a kind that concerns no record with a state.

reason.description: The reason or problem text Runner recorded with the change, where the record serves one, cut at 1,024 bytes; for a discarded cloud signal, the reason Runner gives.

previousRevision.description: trigger.*: the trigger's revision before the change; null for a new trigger. The values of both are the trigger's snapshots, never copied here.

keyIssued.description: trigger.resumed: the event trigger's first key was issued at this revision. The key is in the answer to the request, never here.

nextAt.description: trigger.resumed, for a schedule: its next time; occurrence.retry-scheduled: the time of the occurrence's next attempt.

occurrenceKind.description: An occurrence's admission (from null): the kind of trigger it came from.

scheduledAt.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

missedFrom.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

missedThrough.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

expiresAt.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

deadline.description: occurrence.preparing, for a durable preparation: its deadline.

readyUntil.description: occurrence.ready, for a durable preparation: until when its run may be admitted.

chainSequence.description: run.completed: the sequence of the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, appended in the same transaction.

runtimeDigest.description: release.previewed: the release's Runtime; runner.started: the Runtime this process pinned.

tests.description: release.previewed: the state of the release's saved tests.

request.description: admission.refused: the request refused. A refusal's entry is best effort: if the store cannot write it, the refusal is answered as it was and has no entry.

status.description: admission.refused: the HTTP status the request was answered with. Absent for a cloud signal.

code.description: admission.refused: the error code the request was answered with. Absent for a cloud signal.

coalescedSeconds.description: admission.refused: identical refusals in this many seconds after the entry are not entries.

held.description: journal.began: what the store held when its journal began, none of which has an entry.

attempt.description: The attempt the change closed or kept: on occurrence.retry-scheduled, on an occurrence's change from preparing for a job with a retry policy, and on run.queued from interrupted (a retry), the interrupted attempt kept. An entry that holds it has entryVersion 4.

disposition.description: On run.completed: the run's decision. An entry that holds it has entryVersion 5.

errorClass.description: On run.failed, run.expired and run.interrupted, and on occurrence.failed and occurrence.expired: the record's error class. An entry that holds it has entryVersion 5.

counts.description: On run.completed, run.failed, run.expired and run.interrupted: the run's counts. An entry that holds it has entryVersion 5.

journalBegan.description: When the store's journal began. Nothing before it has an entry, and nothing is back-filled.

next.description: The sequence of the page's last entry, or the cursor given when a forward page is empty (0 when a backward page is empty): the after of the next forward request. It never resets to 0 on a forward page.

more.description: Another page is already available: after a forward page, later entries; after a backward page (tail or before), entries older than the page.

before.description: Only in the answer to a request with tail or before: the sequence of the page's first entry, the before of the request for the next older page (the cursor given, or 0 for the newest page, when the page is empty). Forward answers do not carry it.

profile.description: Explicit Base is required for retained-column conversions. Absent, ordinary legacy behavior and limits apply.

InputMappingV3.description: A dialect document of version 3 (spec/dialect.md sections 4.3 and 4.4): version 2's members but provider, facts and evidence, which version 3 does not carry. A request's version-3 document is kept as written: one Runner would write otherwise (an optional member written empty, or provider, facts or evidence) is refused, so that its digest, the preparation's mappingDigest, is the digest of the document's own canonical bytes. It is read only at source.mapping (input.source.mapping in a preview request and in an event delivery), each member named exactly so: one under a member that is one of those names but for case, or beside such a member, is refused as invalid_source_input. Its sources are bound, or are bound at import (SourceInput.import).

BindingDocument.description: spec/dialect.md section 4.4: binds each unbound source of one published dialect to input profiles of this installation, by id and digest, and changes nothing else: an operation to one profile, and a research source to its AI profile (profile and profileDigest) and a web profile for each web capability it asks for (webProfiles). Its digest is the SHA-256 of its gateway canonical bytes; no preparation holds it.

dialect.description: The digest of the published dialect's gateway canonical bytes.

webProfiles.description: For a research source, REQUIRED: a profile for each web capability it asks for, exactly those, written even when empty.

DialectImport.description: The import step. Runner binds the published dialect with the binding document under this installation's input profiles, refusing by name a dialect that is not of version 3, has no unbound source or is written otherwise than Runner keeps it; a binding for another dialect, that leaves an unbound source unbound, binds a source the dialect does not have or one already bound, or names a member other than a profile's id and digest; and a profile this installation does not hold by that id and digest, of another shape than the source's, or whose adapter is not the source's record. A research source is bound by exactly its AI profile, its digest and its web profiles, the web profiles exactly the web capabilities it asks for (input-malformed otherwise; three web assignments are input-over-bound), each profile of class generated, declaring the capability it is bound for and the source's model (profile-mismatch otherwise). The bound dialect is the published one with each unbound operation's platform, operation, shape and record replaced by the profile, and each unbound research source's three assignment members added, every other member as written. Runner keeps it as the input's mapping and keeps both documents here, as given, beside the run: the operator's record of what was bound, which no preparation holds. Every later preparation of the input, a dispatcher's and verify-run's included, binds them again under the profiles it is given and requires the mapping to be the bound dialect.

SetAsideInputProfile.description: A registered profile Runner set aside when it opened its store: one an earlier Runner admitted and this Runner's admission refuses on its own. Never bound: a binding, job or run that names it is refused as input_profile_set_aside, naming it. A failure of the stored set, such as a malformed row, more than 16 profiles, an ID stored twice or the ID of a configured profile of another definition, still refuses to open the store; a configured profile this Runner refuses still refuses to start.

profile.description: The stored profile, which this Runner's form refuses: its stored bytes, served compacted and JSON-escaped as every answer is. The store's row keeps them exactly.

digest.description: The profile's digest, as a binding to it names it.

reason.description: This Runner's refusal of the profile.

ManualExecutionBinding.description: Private experimental exact canonical typed Release preimage. Read-only binding material grants no registration or execution permission.

ConversionContract.description: Experimental immutable Draft selection. Roles follow the listed order. The complete tuple must equal the installed reviewed package manifest; a caller cannot install a revision, maxima or producer authority. Extended Runner is unsupported.

ConversionCapability.description: Trusted installation metadata, independent of the source selector. Every integer uses a positive non-exponent JSON token. Producer grammar must match the approved source/adapter pin.

profile.description: Explicit Base is required for retained-column conversions. Absent, ordinary legacy behavior and limits apply.
Explicit Base is required for retained-column conversions. Absent, ordinary legacy behavior and limits apply.

ProducerConversionLimits.description: Downward-only caller ceilings derived from the approved producer profile. They grant no producer or installation authority. Retained with durable acquisition intent; resumed intent must match.

bound.description: At most 16 selected profiles, whose stored JSON array is at most 81920 bytes, apart from the 16 ordinary profiles.

ErrorClass.description: The class of a run that ended failed or interrupted, or of an occurrence that ended failed or expired, from a closed list (docs/design/run-results.md, section 3), beside its reason: source, a source acquisition through a Gateway connection failed (no answer, a refusal other than 401 or 403, an answer over its limit, a receipt for another session); preparation, the input could not be read or prepared, or no longer passes its checks (prepared-by-earlier-runner among them); evaluation, the Runtime's evaluation process started and failed, or what it wrote did not pass Runner's checks; configuration, what the work was set up with changed, is not installed or was refused access (profile-set-aside, a release changed before admission, a connection no longer installed, a gateway that refused the acquisition 401 or 403); limit, a time or count bound ended the work (queue-expired, attempt-limit-reached, retry-wait-too-long, a source wait that expired); interrupted, Runner stopped or restarted during the work; internal, Runner's own fault (binding-refused, a release that could not be read, and any failure of a run before the Runtime's evaluation process started, a manual admission authority's reservation or start commitment among them). Every reason code maps to exactly one class. A class says where the failure arose, not whether trying again will help: an acquisition is attempted again by the job's retry policy alone (docs/design/retries.md), and a run only by a caller's retry. Absent on success, on a completed run whatever its disposition, on a skipped, cancelled or waiting occurrence, and on a record that ended before Runner kept it. A class is added only with a change of the design record: a reader may take an unknown class as a newer Runner's.

RunCounts.description: What a finished run's record holds, counted (docs/design/run-results.md, section 2). A run is one evaluation today, so decisions is 1 or 0 and each map holds at most one member; the shape stays right for a run that holds several.

sources.description: The sources the run's preparation records an outcome for (input.preparation.outcomes, the case among them when the mapping reads one). Absent for a run whose input holds no preparation.

decisions.description: The decisions the run's record holds: 1 for a completed run, 0 for any other, an interrupted run among them.

byKind.description: The decisions by disposition kind (outcome, unresolved or not-applicable, as the Runtime wrote it); {} when there are none.

byOutcome.description: The decisions of kind outcome, by outcomeId; {} when there are none.

JournalDisposition.description: The decision of a completed run, as its journal entry names it: the disposition's kind and, for kind outcome, its outcomeId. The pack's reasons and the handoff are the run's to serve.
